long_biography.plain_text:
Lowy was born in Fiľakovo, then part of Czechoslovakia, and survived Nazi persecution in wartime Hungary; his father was murdered after deportation to Auschwitz. As a teenager he travelled to Mandatory Palestine, joined the Haganah and fought in Israel's war of independence. He moved to Australia in 1952 with little formal education and limited English.

In Sydney, Lowy entered a smallgoods business before partnering with fellow immigrant John Saunders in a delicatessen. The pair shifted into property development and opened their first suburban shopping centre in 1959, then listed Westfield the following year. Lowy led its expansion through Australia, the United States and Britain, making shopping centres the foundation of the family's later investment office.
